title: A tetranuclear Er(III)-based cluster with bifunctional properties: Efficient conversion of CO2 and slow magnetic relaxation behavior

material_class.structural_family: tetranuclear Er4 core with μ2-O and μ3-O bridges; Er(III) ions in triangular dodecahedron (D2d) geometry

synthesis.procedure: Er(acac)3·2H2O (0.05 mmol, 0.0495 g), polydentate Schiff-base ligand H4L (0.05 mmol, 0.0138 g), and HNO3 (50 μL) were added to a mixed solution of CH3OH (5 mL) and CH3CN (5 mL) and stirred for about 30 min. The mixed solution was sealed in a 20 mL vial, heated to 70 °C for 24 h under autogenous pressure, then slowly cooled to room temperature. Yellow blocky crystals of 1 were obtained.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal reaction in a sealed 20 mL vial under autogenous pressure
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow cooling to room temperature afforded yellow blocky crystals

properties.summary: Cluster 1 shows slow magnetic relaxation of magnetization under zero dc field, with frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac signals below 13 K but no χ″ peaks, consistent with fast QTM. DC data indicate χMT slightly below the four-Er(III) free-ion value at 300 K, a decrease to 25.76 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, and unsaturated magnetization with magnetic anisotropy.

measurements.name: magnetization M
measurements.conditions: 2.0 K, 70 kOe; field dependence measured below 7.0 K, 0–70 kOe

measurements.name: ac susceptibility slow relaxation
measurements.value: frequency-dependent χ″ signals below 13 K; no χ″ peaks
measurements.conditions: 3.0 Oe ac field, zero dc field
